Subject: Follow-up: PO vs card & procurement next steps

Hi Sarah -

Great to speak earlier - thanks for walking me through FinOpsCo's evaluation goals and the pilot you mentioned. To recap the items that came up and the options for moving the commercial path forward:

1) Payment method constraints
   - You mentioned AP typically requires a PO for vendor payments over $10k, otherwise credit card is acceptable for small pilots.
   - Marketplace purchases are often easiest for quick pilots (card-based), but you prefer vendors to be onboarded for audit purposes.

2) Vendor onboarding
   - FinOpsCo will need a completed vendor form + W-9 and typically completes onboarding within ~2 weeks once docs are received.

3) Next steps I can take from our side
   - Attachments: sending a Redwood W-9 and our vendor onboarding stub (attached). Please share your vendor questionnaire if you have one.
   - If you prefer a PO path, we can prepare a standard quote + DocuSign for signatures and support your procurement team through onboarding.
   - If you prefer a marketplace purchase for the pilot, I can confirm card-based pricing and provide billing details to your AP.

Can you confirm:
- The AP contact (email) we should work with to get a PO generated?
- Whether you prefer to run the pilot via marketplace (card) or start via contract + PO?
- Any internal timeline targets for onboarding or pilot start?

Looping in Lauren (cc) to draft the quote/options depending on your preference. Happy to jump on a short call with Tom (procurement) if useful.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Marissa -

Thanks for the summary and for sending the W-9. Quick answers below: 

- AP contact: ap@finopsco.com (cc'ed). Tom Riley is our procurement lead and can help with PO questions.
- Policy: For new vendors, AP requires a completed vendor questionnaire + W-9 before we can set them up. For contract sizes > $10k per invoice we require a PO. For smaller pilots (under that threshold) we will typically allow card payment if it goes through our procurement review.
- Marketplace: We do prefer marketplace purchases for small pilots because they generate an auditable invoice and keep the payment workflow simple, but our internal policy means we still need vendors listed and approved in our vendor registry for tracking.
- Timeline: If we get the vendor questionnaire + W-9 this week, procurement estimates ~10 business days to complete onboarding and have a vendor record. PO issuance could follow in that timeframe, depending on internal approvals.

I'll start the vendor questionnaire and loop AP to confirm whether they'll approve a card for an initial $5k pilot. If AP is OK, we can push the pilot through faster via card/marketplace. If not, we'll proceed with PO + contract.

I'll follow up with a short note once AP confirms.

Best,
Sarah Jenkins
Head of Procurement Programs, FinOpsCo
